import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly correlated features (|r| >= 0.6)
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    high_corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                high_corr_pairs.append((feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]))
    
    # Group correlated features into modules using hierarchical clustering
    if not high_corr_pairs:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Create adjacency matrix for clustering
    all_features = set()
    for a, b in high_corr_pairs:
        all_features.add(a)
        all_features.add(b)
    
    feature_list = sorted(list(all_features))
    n_features = len(feature_list)
    
    adj_matrix = np.zeros((n_features, n_features))
    for a, b in high_corr_pairs:
        i, j = feature_list.index(a), feature_list.index(b)
        adj_matrix[i,j] = adj_matrix[j,i] = 1
    
    # Cluster features based on correlation
    clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(n_clusters=1, linkage='complete')
    clusters = clustering.fit_predict(adj_matrix)
    
    # Get the main module (most correlated features)
    module_features = [feature_list[i] for i in range(n_features) if clusters[i] == 0]
    
    # Compute weighted score using t-statistics as weights
    loadings = {}
    for fid in module_features:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        t_stat = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx], feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx]).statistic
        loadings[fid] = t_stat
    
    # Select top features by absolute t-statistic for drivers
    sorted_features = sorted(loadings.keys(), key=lambda x: abs(loadings[x]), reverse=True)
    drivers = tuple(sorted_features[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(sorted_features))])
    
    # Include all module features in regression
    columns = tuple(module_features)
    products = ()
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
